title: Why Spending Too Little Could Backfire on Democrats

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即便是在黑胶唱片时代，我还在夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每晚你都要带着300件最珍贵的收藏去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: When Democrats first set out to expand the social safety net,
sentences.zh: 当民主党人最初着手扩大社会安全网时，

sentences.en: they envisioned a piece of legislation as transformational as what the party had achieved in the 1960s and hoped that in the process,
sentences.zh: 他们设想了一项具有变革意义的立法，其规模堪比该党在20世纪60年代取得的成就，并希望在此过程中，

sentences.en: they'd win back the working-class voters the party had since loSt.
sentences.zh: 他们能赢回那些已经流失的工薪阶层选民。

sentences.en: But now that they're on the brink of reaching a deal, the question is whether the enormous cuts and compromises they've made will make it impossible to accomplish either.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们即将达成协议，问题在于，他们所做出的巨大削减和妥协是否会使这两项目标都无法实现。

sentences.en: I spoke to my colleague, congressional reporter Jonathan Weissman.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事，国会记者乔纳森·韦斯曼。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, October 26th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月26日，星期二。

sentences.en: Jonathan, as this bill was originally conceived,
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，正如这项法案最初构想的那样，

sentences.en: it was a $6 trillion act of social spending that would have been the most significant expansion of the country's social safety net since President Lyndon Johnson's Great Society in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 这是一项6万亿美元的社会支出法案，本将成为自林登·约翰逊总统在20世纪60年代提出“伟大社会”以来，美国社会安全网最重大的扩张。

sentences.en: And I know that you're a student of American history.
sentences.zh: 我知道你是一位美国历史研究者。

sentences.en: So remind us of the context in which that monumental act of spending occurred and what it was all about.
sentences.zh: 那么，请提醒我们那项里程碑式的支出法案是在什么样的背景下产生的，以及它的核心内容是什么。

sentences.en: Well, some of the context actually might sound familiar.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一些背景听起来可能很耳熟。

sentences.en: Then, as now, tax cuts had just been passed that largely accrued to the benefit of the rich.
sentences.zh: 当时和现在一样，刚刚通过的减税政策主要让富人受益。

sentences.en: And the economy was growing really well writ large.
sentences.zh: 而且从大局来看，当时的经济增长非常强劲。

sentences.en: In fact, when Lyndon Johnson took over the presidency, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当林登·约翰逊接任总统时，美国

sentences.en: economy had just grown by 10%.
sentences.zh: 经济刚刚增长了10%。

sentences.en: That is a huge burst of growth.
sentences.zh: 那是一次巨大的增长爆发。

sentences.en: And right now, we're also seeing an economy in recovery.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我们也正处于经济复苏之中。

sentences.en: And then, as now, what the president was seeing was a society growing more and more unequal.
sentences.zh: 而且当时和现在一样，总统所看到的是一个日益不平等的社会。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, many Americans live on the outskirts of hope.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，许多美国人生活在希望的边缘。

sentences.en: Johnson looks around and he sees...
sentences.zh: 约翰逊环顾四周，他看到了……

sentences.en: Some because of their poverty and some because of their color.
sentences.zh: 有些人是因为贫穷，有些人是因为肤色。

sentences.en: And all too many because of both.
sentences.zh: 而太多人是因为两者兼有。

sentences.en: Entrenched poverty and real pain out there.
sentences.zh: 根深蒂固的贫困和真实的痛苦。

sentences.en: Replace their despair.
sentences.zh: 取代他们的绝望。

sentences.en: Senior citizens who have no health care whatsoever, who are dying in their homes.
sentences.zh: 那些没有任何医疗保障、在家里等死的老年人。

sentences.en: He sees people in Appalachia who are literally starving.
sentences.zh: 他看到阿巴拉契亚地区的人们正在挨饿。

sentences.en: He sees poverty amidst riches that would break anybody's heart.
sentences.zh: 他看到富裕之中的贫困，这足以让任何人感到心碎。

sentences.en: And this administration today, here and now, declares unconditional war on poverty in America.
sentences.zh: 今天，此时此刻，本届政府宣布对美国的贫困发动无条件战争。

sentences.en: And he says, the government needs to step in.
sentences.zh: 他说，政府需要介入。

sentences.en: The richest nation on earth can afford to win it.
sentences.zh: 地球上最富有的国家有能力赢得这场战争。

sentences.en: At a time of prosperity, at a moment where we can afford it, we need to step in and make sure there is a real safety net for the bottom of the bottom of this country.
sentences.zh: 在繁荣时期，在我们负担得起的时候，我们需要介入，确保为这个国家的底层民众提供真正的安全网。

sentences.en: And so...
sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: We have the opportunity to move not only toward the rich society and the powerful society, but upward to the great society.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅有机会迈向富裕和强大的社会，更有机会迈向伟大的社会。

sentences.en: What Lyndon Johnson came up with was a series of programs that lumped together, he called, the great society.
sentences.zh: 林登·约翰逊提出了一系列计划，他将这些计划统称为“伟大社会”。

sentences.en: The great society rests on abundance and liberty for all.
sentences.zh: “伟大社会”建立在人人享有富足与自由的基础之上。

sentences.en: It demands an end to poverty and racial injustice.
sentences.zh: 它要求终结贫困和种族不公正。

sentences.en: To which we're totally committed in our time.
sentences.zh: 这是我们这个时代全力以赴的目标。

sentences.en: And tell us how those programs worked.
sentences.zh: 请告诉我们这些计划是如何运作的。

sentences.en: So, for those old people who had no access to doctors and medicine, there was Medicare.
sentences.zh: 对于那些无法获得医生和药物的老年人，有了医疗保险（Medicare）。

sentences.en: To the poor who had no access to doctors and medicine, there was Medicaid.
sentences.zh: 对于那些无法获得医生和药物的穷人，有了医疗补助（Medicaid）。

sentences.en: To those really struggling with food, to put food on the table, there was the creation of the food stamp program.
sentences.zh: 对于那些在温饱线上挣扎的人，建立了食品券计划。

sentences.en: There was the expansion of welfare.
sentences.zh: 还有福利制度的扩张。

sentences.en: Now, there had been some welfare programs, but they didn't go very far.
sentences.zh: 虽然之前也有一些福利项目，但覆盖范围并不广。

sentences.en: And Johnson wanted a much more expansive welfare program to make sure that people weren't in abject poverty.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊希望建立一个更广泛的福利计划，以确保人们不会陷入赤贫。

sentences.en: And to poor children, who had no access to decent schools, he created Head Start, which actually, finally, gave poor children a way in to preschool.
sentences.zh: 对于那些无法进入体面学校的贫困儿童，他创立了“启智计划”（Head Start），这终于让贫困儿童有了接受学前教育的途径。

sentences.en: And then the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, for the first time,
sentences.zh: 然后是《中小学教育法》，这是第一次，

sentences.en: began sending money to the poorest school districts from Washington to make sure that there was at least a basic education for the poorest children.
sentences.zh: 开始从华盛顿向最贫困的学区拨款，以确保最贫困的孩子至少能接受基础教育。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: This is quite a liSt.
sentences.zh: 这真是一份长长的清单。

sentences.en: Medicare, Medicaid, food stamps, welfare, Head Start, all of that is a result of the Great Society.
sentences.zh: 医疗保险、医疗补助、食品券、福利、启智计划，所有这些都是“伟大社会”的成果。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The social safety net that we think of right now was created in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 我们现在所认为的社会安全网就是在那时创建的。

sentences.en: And Jonathan, what do we understand the effectiveness of the Great Society to have been?
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，我们应该如何理解“伟大社会”的成效？

sentences.en: What is its legacy?
sentences.zh: 它的遗产是什么？

sentences.en: The Great Society, in some sense, really did work.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，“伟大社会”确实奏效了。

sentences.en: It left a tremendous number of Americans out of abject poverty.
sentences.zh: 它让无数美国人摆脱了赤贫。

sentences.en: And it created a floor under which, by and large, Americans don't slip.
sentences.zh: 它建立了一个底线，绝大多数美国人不会跌落到这个底线之下。

sentences.en: If you want help, if you need food, if you need education, if you need a doctor, and you're very poor, you should be able to get one thanks to the Great Society.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要帮助，如果你需要食物、教育或医生，而你又非常贫穷，多亏了“伟大社会”，你应该能够得到这些保障。

sentences.en: And Jonathan, what were the political consequences of the Great Society?
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，那么“伟大社会”带来的政治后果是什么？

sentences.en: The Great Society actually proved to be very popular.
sentences.zh: “伟大社会”实际上非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: The proof in the pudding is how long these programs have lasted.
sentences.zh: 事实胜于雄辩，这些计划持续了这么久就是证明。

sentences.en: Food stamps, Medicare, Medicaid.
sentences.zh: 食品券、医疗保险、医疗补助。

sentences.en: Nobody is talking about doing away with these programs because they have become embedded in our society and accepted broadly by the American voter.
sentences.zh: 没有人谈论废除这些计划，因为它们已经融入了我们的社会，并被美国选民广泛接受。

sentences.en: And Americans accept that we need a floor under all of us to make sure that we don't fall into abject poverty.
sentences.zh: 美国人认同我们需要一个底线，以确保我们所有人都不会陷入赤贫。

sentences.en: But, you know, jump forward 50 years and what we have seen is great new strains emerging in our society, in the working poor and the middle class,
sentences.zh: 但是，快进50年，我们看到社会中出现了新的巨大压力，工薪阶层和中产阶级

sentences.en: which have struggled to keep up as the rich have bolted forward.
sentences.zh: 在富人飞速前进的同时，他们却在苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: And the Democrats looked at that, Joe Biden looked at that situation and again said, it's time for government to do something.
sentences.zh: 民主党人看到了这一点，乔·拜登看到了这种情况，再次表示，政府是时候采取行动了。

sentences.en: That this great stagnation among the working class has to be prodded forward.
sentences.zh: 工薪阶层的这种巨大停滞必须得到推动。

sentences.en: That we can't keep doing the same thing that we've been doing for 50 years and hope that those struggling will finally find their way to more affluence and to more stability.
sentences.zh: 我们不能再重复过去50年的做法，并指望那些挣扎中的人们最终能找到通往富裕和稳定的道路。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And their solution was a new wave of social spending, but not one just focused on poverty, but instead building off the base of the Great Society and focusing, as you just said,
sentences.zh: 他们的解决方案是新一轮的社会支出，但不仅仅关注贫困，而是以“伟大社会”为基础，正如你刚才所说，

sentences.en: on the working class and the middle class.
sentences.zh: 重点关注工薪阶层和中产阶级。

sentences.en: And interestingly, many of these voters that the Democrats are seeking to extend these benefits to are the voters they have lost in the years since the Great Society.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，民主党试图将这些福利扩展到的许多选民，正是他们在“伟大社会”之后流失的选民。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The white working class has drifted to the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 白人工薪阶层已经转向了共和党。

sentences.en: And the white working class, that discontented group that has stagnated over the last 30 years, that's the group that these programs are really aimed at.
sentences.zh: 而白人工薪阶层，那个在过去30年里停滞不前、心怀不满的群体，正是这些计划真正瞄准的对象。

sentences.en: And what exactly was the Democratic plan to do that?
sentences.zh: 那么民主党实现这一目标的具体计划是什么？

sentences.en: So what the Democrats had in mind is a government program that would give the working class and the middle class access to the kind of benefits that white collar workers and the affluent just take for granted.
sentences.zh: 民主党的构想是一个政府计划，让工薪阶层和中产阶级能够获得白领和富裕阶层视为理所当然的福利。

sentences.en: So for pregnant women and for new parents, there would be a new family and medical leave component for parents trying to get back into the workforce after a child,
sentences.zh: 对于孕妇和新手父母，将有一项新的家庭和医疗假计划；对于生育后试图重返职场的父母，

sentences.en: there would be rich new subsidies for child care.
sentences.zh: 将会有丰厚的托儿补贴。

sentences.en: Once that child reached two or three, there would be universal access to pre-kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 一旦孩子长到两三岁，将普及学前教育。

sentences.en: And then once they've gotten through school, there would be universal community college.
sentences.zh: 当他们完成学业后，将普及社区大学教育。

sentences.en: There would be job training throughout their lives.
sentences.zh: 终身都会有职业培训。

sentences.en: And then when they get older, there would be help for people to help their parents get elder care.
sentences.zh: 当他们年长时，将会有帮助他们照顾父母的养老护理支持。

sentences.en: And then once they enrolled in Medicare, there would be an expansion of Medicare services to cover vision, hearing and dental.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们加入医疗保险，医疗保险服务将扩大到涵盖视力、听力和牙科。

sentences.en: So the Democrats envisioned a real reweaving of the social safety net, really at every stage of a person's life, cradle to grave.
sentences.zh: 因此，民主党设想的是对社会安全网进行真正的重构，真正覆盖一个人从摇篮到坟墓的每个阶段。

sentences.en: So if the Great Society was about this idea that there would be a floor that all Americans could stand on,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果说“伟大社会”的理念是为所有美国人提供一个立足的底线，

sentences.en: would it be fair to say that this bill seeks to create a kind of staircase that would allow Americans to make it from, if you'll indulge this metaphor a bit more,
sentences.zh: 那么是否可以公平地说，这项法案旨在建造一种阶梯，让美国人能够从——如果你允许我继续使用这个比喻——

sentences.en: the ground floor to maybe the second or third floor?
sentences.zh: 底层迈向二楼或三楼？

sentences.en: It's about the possibility of upward mobility and the belief that American society has become so stratified that government intervention is really the only way to make that possible because hard work alone is so rarely enough.
sentences.zh: 这关乎向上流动的可能性，以及一种信念：美国社会已经变得如此分层，以至于政府干预是实现这一目标的唯一途径，因为仅靠努力工作往往是不够的。

sentences.en: This bill was about constructing a social safety net to make sure that all of those terrible mishaps that afflict us all, whether it's a sick child, a sick parent,
sentences.zh: 这项法案旨在构建一个社会安全网，以确保所有困扰我们的可怕不幸，无论是孩子生病、父母生病，

sentences.en: whether it's a difficult pregnancy, that they will not derail a person's hope to ever reach the real middle class and to reach stability.
sentences.zh: 还是怀孕困难，都不会阻碍一个人进入真正的中产阶级并获得稳定的希望。

sentences.en: Okay, so that was the grand intention of all of this, to build on the Great Society and create this greater society with more social mobility.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这一切的宏伟意图就是建立在“伟大社会”的基础上，创造一个具有更多社会流动性的更伟大社会。

sentences.en: That was the intention.
sentences.zh: 这就是初衷。

sentences.en: And then reality struck.
sentences.zh: 然后现实给了他们一记重击。

sentences.en: A 50-50 Senate, a majority in the House in which three dissenters could derail it.
sentences.zh: 50对50的参议院，以及在众议院中只要有三个人反对就可能导致法案搁浅。

sentences.en: And suddenly the Democrats came to the realization that their grand vision could not survive the politics of the United States Congress.
sentences.zh: 民主党人突然意识到，他们的宏伟愿景无法在复杂的美国国会政治中存活。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过nytimes.com进行部分采访的直播，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: So, Jonathan, let's talk about what happened once reality struck, once Democrats realized they had no margin for error, once they began fighting over the size of this all.
sentences.zh: 那么，乔纳森，让我们谈谈现实发生后，当民主党人意识到他们没有犯错的余地，当他们开始为法案的规模争吵时，发生了什么。

sentences.en: And what the current state of the bill now is as a result.
sentences.zh: 以及该法案目前的状态如何。

sentences.en: I know it has been stripped way down.
sentences.zh: 我知道它已经被大幅削减了。

sentences.en: So, a vision that at one time foresaw spending $6 trillion over 10 years was first cut down to $3.5 trillion, a level that was difficult for some Democrats to accept,
sentences.zh: 曾经设想在10年内支出6万亿美元的愿景，首先被削减到了3.5万亿美元，这是一个让一些民主党人难以接受的水平，

sentences.en: but one that President Biden accepted.
sentences.zh: 但拜登总统接受了。

sentences.en: And now the deal that Democrats are about to announce will be somewhere around $1.5 trillion, a fraction of that original $6 trillion price tag.
sentences.zh: 而现在，民主党即将宣布的协议金额将在1.5万亿美元左右，仅为最初6万亿美元价格标签的一小部分。

sentences.en: So, when we think about that cradle-to-grave ambition of this bill, how is that being affected by these trillions of dollars in cuts?
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们想到这项法案从摇篮到坟墓的雄心时，数万亿美元的削减是如何影响它的？

sentences.en: Does it mean that this bill is no longer capturing the full span of an American life, or is it reducing the spending at each stage, or what?
sentences.zh: 这意味着该法案不再涵盖美国人生活的全貌，还是在每个阶段都减少了支出，或者是什么情况？

sentences.en: Really, all of the above.
sentences.zh: 实际上，以上皆是。

sentences.en: For instance, remember I talked to you about universal access to community college.
sentences.zh: 例如，记得我跟你谈过普及社区大学吗？

sentences.en: That's gone.
sentences.zh: 那已经没了。

sentences.en: That's not even in the bill anymore.
sentences.zh: 那甚至不在法案里了。

sentences.en: Or, I talked about access to child care.
sentences.zh: 或者，我谈到的托儿服务。

sentences.en: Well, that child care access is now going to be limited probably to people with incomes up to $60,000.
sentences.zh: 现在，托儿服务的覆盖范围可能仅限于收入在6万美元以下的人群。

sentences.en: And, you know, for a working class person in, say, an affluent part of New Jersey, that $60,000 cutoff is really going to hurt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于新泽西州富裕地区的工薪阶层来说，6万美元的门槛真的会造成伤害。

sentences.en: If you're earning $65,000, you're probably still struggling with child care.
sentences.zh: 如果你赚6.5万美元，你可能仍然在为托儿问题挣扎。

sentences.en: And there's also the issue of longevity.
sentences.zh: 还有一个长期性的问题。

sentences.en: In the COVID relief bill that passed in March, there was a revolutionary new program.
sentences.zh: 在3月份通过的疫情救助法案中，有一个革命性的新项目。

sentences.en: It was a $300 income support per child that many, many families were getting.
sentences.zh: 那是每名儿童每月300美元的收入支持，许多家庭都从中受益。

sentences.en: It was only for one year.
sentences.zh: 它只持续了一年。

sentences.en: But this bill envisioned making that virtually permanent.
sentences.zh: 但这项法案设想将其变为永久性项目。

sentences.en: At least for six years, families with children would see this $300 showing up in their bank accounts every month.
sentences.zh: 至少在六年内，有孩子的家庭每个月都能在银行账户里看到这300美元。

sentences.en: Well, because of these cuts, they're talking about extending that child credit for only one more year.
sentences.zh: 然而，由于这些削减，他们现在只讨论将儿童税收抵免再延长一年。

sentences.en: And that's going to have real impact because families can't count on a program like that to vault them into a more stable economic life if they think it's just going to evaporate in a year.
sentences.zh: 这会产生真正的影响，因为如果家庭认为这种项目一年后就会消失，他们就无法指望它能帮助自己进入更稳定的经济生活。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It sounds like you're saying that there are three distinct things going on here as this bill gets stripped back.
sentences.zh: 听起来你是说，随着法案被不断削减，这里发生了三件截然不同的事情。

sentences.en: The first is that some things are just altogether gone.
sentences.zh: 第一，有些项目完全消失了。

sentences.en: The second is that, like the Great Society, the bill would be more focused on the neediest, poorest Americans and once again wouldn't really address the working and middle class.
sentences.zh: 第二，就像“伟大社会”一样，该法案将更多地关注最贫困的美国人，而再次无法真正解决工薪阶层和中产阶级的问题。

sentences.en: And the third is that the time frame for these programs, in many cases, would be very short and consolidated.
sentences.zh: 第三，在许多情况下，这些项目的时间框架会非常短且被压缩。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And those time frame issues are very big because instead of a new benefit that people can count on,
sentences.zh: 这些时间框架的问题非常严重，因为人们得到的不是可以依赖的新福利，

sentences.en: they're really looking at just kind of a temporary bonus to get them through the next 12 to 24 months.
sentences.zh: 而只是一种临时的奖金，帮助他们度过接下来的12到24个月。

sentences.en: I'm interested in the implications of that because thinking back to what you said, Jonathan, about the Great Society as an example, or even more recently, the Affordable Care Act,
sentences.zh: 我对其中的影响很感兴趣，因为回想一下你提到的“伟大社会”的例子，或者更近期的《平价医疗法案》，

sentences.en: we know that it took a lot of time for people to become accustomed to these prograMs.
sentences.zh: 我们知道人们花了很多时间才习惯这些项目。

sentences.en: I mean, famously, many Americans who had stood to benefit most from the Affordable Care Act, they hated it when it was first announced as Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，众所周知，许多本应从《平价医疗法案》中受益最多的美国人，在它最初以“奥巴马医改”的名义宣布时，非常讨厌它。

sentences.en: But as it became part of their lives and they saw its benefits, it grew in popularity and now it's seen as a big part of what flipped the House to Democrats in 2018.
sentences.zh: 但随着它成为他们生活的一部分，他们看到了它的好处，它的受欢迎程度随之上升，现在它被视为2018年民主党夺回众议院控制权的重要原因。

sentences.en: To put it simply, programs take time and they need time.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，这些项目需要时间，也确实需要时间。

sentences.en: And what you're now saying is that a lot of these programs are not going to have much time.
sentences.zh: 而你现在的意思是，这些项目中的许多将不会有太多时间。

sentences.en: Yeah, the Democrats, the optimistic ones, think that even if Republicans take control of the House next year or maybe even the Senate,
sentences.zh: 没错，乐观的民主党人认为，即使共和党明年控制了众议院，甚至可能控制参议院，

sentences.en: that somehow these programs will be so popular that even a Republican Congress would have to re-up them.
sentences.zh: 这些项目也会因为太受欢迎，以至于共和党控制的国会也不得不延长它们。

sentences.en: But there is a really, really, really, really high probability that a program that lasts one or two years will just be allowed to expire at the end of that time limit.
sentences.zh: 但一个只持续一两年的项目，在期限结束时被直接叫停的可能性真的、真的、真的、非常高。

sentences.en: Because the fact is, a lot of Americans won't even have noticed that program is helping them yet.
sentences.zh: 因为事实是，很多美国人甚至还没注意到这些项目正在为他们提供帮助。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They might not have any clue how to have accessed that child care money, how to get to that universal pre-K, because, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们可能根本不知道如何获取那笔儿童保育资金，也不知道如何享受全民学前教育，因为，你知道的，

sentences.en: it takes time for people to understand how to get a government benefit.
sentences.zh: 人们需要时间来了解如何获得政府福利。

sentences.en: It will not have really become enmeshed in their economic livelihoods.
sentences.zh: 这些项目还没能真正融入他们的经济生活。

sentences.en: How many programs originally envisioned in this Democratic spending bill as plans that would last a really long time are now going to be funded for just a year or two and not be likely to achieve the longevity that you're talking about?
sentences.zh: 在这项民主党支出法案中，最初设想为长期计划的项目，现在有多少只会获得一两年的资助，且不太可能实现你所说的长期性？

sentences.en: Virtually all of them.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有项目。

sentences.en: They will all expire in the next two to three years, some in one year.
sentences.zh: 它们都将在未来两到三年内到期，有些甚至一年内就会到期。

sentences.en: In which case Democrats are not really going to have a chance to show Americans that these programs work and they're not very likely to get that much credit for them.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，民主党人实际上将没有机会向美国人证明这些项目是有效的，他们也不太可能因此获得多少功劳。

sentences.en: I mean, as you said, it took many, many years for the Affordable Care Act to really register as a base support for health care in this country.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如你所说，平价医疗法案在这个国家真正作为医疗保健的基础支持发挥作用，花费了许多许多年。

sentences.en: And in this case,
sentences.zh: 而在这种情况下，

sentences.en: this vision of a new social safety net to propel the struggling working class into a more affluent middle class really won't have time to have really taken root before Republicans could just let it expire,
sentences.zh: 这种旨在推动挣扎中的工薪阶层进入更富裕中产阶级的社会安全网新愿景，在共和党人将其废除之前，根本没有时间真正扎根，

sentences.en: before President Biden even gets to run for re-election.
sentences.zh: 甚至在拜登总统有机会竞选连任之前。

sentences.en: Jonathan, as you're talking, it occurs to me that counterintuitively, greater government spending, the original version of this bill,
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，在你说话的时候，我突然想到一个反直觉的观点，即政府增加支出，也就是这项法案的最初版本，

sentences.en: it might have been one of the most powerful ways for the Democrats to try to win back the voters that they have lost in recent years or are still at risk of losing.
sentences.zh: 这可能是民主党人试图赢回近年来失去或仍有流失风险的选民的最有力方式之一。

sentences.en: Because even though we think of more moderate and conservative voters as opposing government spending, the benefits of this bill, quite uniquely,
sentences.zh: 因为尽管我们认为温和派和保守派选民反对政府支出，但这项法案的益处非常独特，

sentences.en: could have so directly benefited those voters that it could have been like another version of Obamacare,
sentences.zh: 它本可以直接惠及那些选民，以至于它可能成为另一个版本的奥巴马医改，

sentences.en: but even more transformational to the lives of working and middle class Americans.
sentences.zh: 甚至对工薪阶层和中产阶级美国人的生活产生更深远的变革。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Democrats saw the original conception of this bill as a way for government to make a real difference in the lives of working and middle class Americans.
sentences.zh: 民主党人最初将这项法案构想为政府改善工薪阶层和中产阶级美国人生活的一种方式。

sentences.en: But perversely, by shrinking it down to ostensibly make it more palatable to conservative voters, Democrats might be making it less politically efficacious.
sentences.zh: 但讽刺的是，为了表面上让保守派选民更容易接受而缩减规模，民主党人可能反而降低了它的政治效力。

sentences.en: Because if you know that the Democrats passed this big bill that's spending a lot of money, but you don't see it, you don't get a chance to really feel the impact,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你知道民主党通过了这个花费巨资的大法案，但你却看不到它，也没有机会真正感受到它的影响，

sentences.en: then you're really susceptible to the countercharge that will be coming from Republicans.
sentences.zh: 那么你就很容易受到共和党人随之而来的反击的影响。

sentences.en: And you can just imagine the ads.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一下那些广告。

sentences.en: Democrats spent a trillion and a half dollars of your hard-earned money.
sentences.zh: 民主党人花了你们一万五千亿美元的血汗钱。

sentences.en: And who got that money?
sentences.zh: 谁拿到了这笔钱？

sentences.en: Not you.
sentences.zh: 不是你。

sentences.en: And that could be a line of attack that could really ring true to people who didn't really understand what the benefits were.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不了解这些福利到底是什么的人来说，这可能是一个非常有说服力的攻击点。

sentences.en: And those benefits are already about to expire.
sentences.zh: 而且这些福利很快就要到期了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well, let me ask you a provocative question, then.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我问你一个挑衅性的问题。

sentences.en: Is there a case to be made that $1.5 trillion is more wasteful than $3.5 or $6 trillion when we think about this policy?
sentences.zh: 当我们考虑这项政策时，是否有理由认为1.5万亿美元比3.5万亿或6万亿美元更浪费？

sentences.en: I think there's a case to be made that in its purest form, in its conception, this bill may well have been transformational,
sentences.zh: 我认为有理由认为，在其最纯粹的形式和构想中，这项法案很可能具有变革性，

sentences.en: not just to society and the social safety network, but also politically, because it would be a true,
sentences.zh: 不仅是对社会和社会安全网，而且在政治上也是如此，因为它将是民主党人赢回白人、挣扎中的工薪阶层忠诚的真正、

sentences.en: tangible step that Democrats would make toward winning back the allegiance of the white, struggling, working class.
sentences.zh: 切实的一步。

sentences.en: But in its much smaller form, not only will it be less effective, it could actually come back to haunt the Democrats politically because it gives the Republicans a weapon.
sentences.zh: 但在其规模缩小后，它不仅效果会大打折扣，甚至可能在政治上反噬民主党，因为它给了共和党一个武器。

sentences.en: And so, if and when those potential Republican ads that I mentioned before start to run and they say,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我之前提到的那些潜在的共和党广告开始投放，他们说，

sentences.en: Democrats spent a trillion and a half dollars of your hard-earned money, and on what?
sentences.zh: 民主党人花了你们一万五千亿美元的血汗钱，花在什么地方了？

sentences.en: Now, that question to the white working class might come back with an answer.
sentences.zh: 现在，对于白人工薪阶层来说，这个问题可能会得到一个回答。

sentences.en: I didn't see any of it.
sentences.zh: 我什么都没看到。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，免费获取30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Even if you're looking for free elections and democracy.
sentences.zh: 即使你追求的是自由选举和民主。

sentences.en: Instead, Sudanese military leaders appear to have abandoned the power sharing system to protect their own power.
sentences.zh: 相反，苏丹军方领导人似乎为了保护自己的权力而放弃了权力分享制度。

sentences.en: In response to the coup, thousands of protesters flooded into the streets of Sudan's capital, Khartoum.
sentences.zh: 作为对政变的回应，成千上万的抗议者涌入了苏丹首都喀土穆的街头。

sentences.en: Soon after, the military turned off the country's internet, making it impossible to monitor the military's reaction to the protests.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，军方切断了全国的互联网，使得人们无法监测军方对抗议活动的反应。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Stella Tan, Daniel Guimet, Rob Zipko, and Chelsea Daniel, with help from Rachel Quester.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由Stella Tan、Daniel Guimet、Rob Zipko和Chelsea Daniel制作，Rachel Quester提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Tobin and M.J.
sentences.zh: 节目由Lisa Tobin和M.J.编辑，

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn, engineered by Chris Wood, and contains original music from Marian Lozano and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: Davis-Lynn负责音频工程，并包含Marian Lozano和Dan Powell的原创音乐。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的Jim Brunberg和Ben Landsberg创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《Metro》的最新一期节目中，我和Sarah Koenig将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你收听播客的地方订阅收听。

sentences.en: Let's see you next.
sentences.zh: 下次见。

sentences.en: Let's see you next time.
sentences.zh: 下次见。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
